The Ineffable Task of Standing on a Hill

I stood at the top of the hill, wind whipping my hair into a frenzy as the world spread out before me like a fractured, rain-soaked canvas. I had 100 words to start, but my brain, in its customary rebellion against sanity, decided to just have 1005. 

It started pouring. The grey skies unleashed a deluge that had the hill struggling to stay remnant of its brief, poorly-lit spring fragment. Droplets hit the mirror-smoothed surface of a distant pond, trigerring a ripples of questions I'd been trying to hold off, worried that my nomadic character wasn't quite apt for a ones-and-done misfortune akin to oddly pale statutes thought.
